column1: # ZAP baseline scan rules for .github/workflows/zap.yml (zap-baseline.py -c).
# Format: rule ID <TAB> IGNORE|WARN|FAIL <TAB> (rule name). Lines starting with # are comments.
# Rules not listed here keep their default action, WARN. The workflow passes -I, so only
# FAIL rules fail the job; WARN results are still listed in the job log and the report.
# FAIL: protections the app has today. A match means a regression.
# Every response must keep X-Frame-Options or CSP frame-ancestors.
# Every response must keep X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff.
# APP_DEBUG must stay off: no stack traces or debug messages in responses.
# Apache hides its version (ServerTokens Prod); a version string here is a regression.
# PHP must not announce itself in an X-Powered-By header.

column1: # Every HTML page must send a Content-Security-Policy.
# Session and XSRF cookies must keep a SameSite attribute.
# CORS must not allow arbitrary origins.
# Every form must keep its CSRF token.
# Error pages must not leak exception details.
# INFO: informational rules that describe the app rather than a weakness. Listed as INFO so
# they stay in the report without being counted as warnings.
# Pages are sent with Cache-Control: no-cache, private, so shared caches do not store them.
# Notes that /login is a login form.
# Notes that the laravel_starter_session cookie is a session cookie.
# IGNORE: false positives for this app, each checked by hand.
# Only XSRF-TOKEN lacks HttpOnly. Laravel sets it so JavaScript can read it; it is a CSRF
# token, not a credential. The session and laravel_token cookies are HttpOnly, which
# tests/e2e/security.spec.js checks.
# The 302 bodies are the standard Symfony "Redirecting to <url>" page and contain only the target URL.
# Only raised for static JavaScript files. Permissions-Policy applies to documents, and every
# HTML page sends it (checked by tests/e2e/security.spec.js).
